evidence.role: Dependency retrieval is grounded in the verified 9702_t01_cm02_l03 handoff; no new P2 demand is claimed

hints: Replace milli with its power-of-ten multiplier.
A duration names one of the five base quantities from the previous lesson.

walkthrough.text: Milli means 10^-3, so 4.8 ms = 4.8 x 10^-3 s.
In decimal form this is 0.0048 s.
A duration measures time, whose SI base unit is the second.

ai_rubric.observable: Converts 4.8 ms to 4.8 x 10^-3 s or 0.0048 s
Identifies time as the SI base quantity measured by a duration

evidence.role: The mapped leaf directly grounds recall of force in SI base-unit form; the options and wording are original

hints: Build force from mass multiplied by acceleration.
Acceleration has one length factor and two inverse time factors.

walkthrough.text: Mass has unit kg and acceleration has unit m s^-2.
Multiplying gives kg m s^-2.
Therefore option B is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects kg m s^-2 as the SI base-unit form of force

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground forming a derived unit from a quotient; the density context and distractors are original

hints: Volume has unit m^3.
A denominator can be written using a negative power.

walkthrough.text: Mass has unit kg and volume has unit m^3.
Mass divided by volume gives kg/m^3.
Writing the denominator with a negative power gives kg m^-3, so A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects kg m^-3 as the SI base-unit form of density

evidence.role: The mapped leaf grounds deriving an unfamiliar constant's base units from a supplied force model; all symbols and model details are newly authored

hints: Rearrange the model to make k the subject.
Combine the area and speed units before subtracting their powers from the force units.

walkthrough.text: Rearrange F = kAv to k = F/(Av).
The denominator has unit (m^2)(m s^-1) = m^3 s^-1.
Divide kg m s^-2 by m^3 s^-1 to get kg m^(1-3) s^(-2-(-1)) = kg m^-2 s^-1.
Therefore option A is correct.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects kg m^-2 s^-1 as the SI base-unit form of k

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground deriving force, stress and power units from supplied relationships; the linked energy-power route is original

hints: Replace N before collecting the metre powers.
For power, dividing by another second reduces the time exponent by one.

walkthrough.text: Complete part (a) by multiplying force units by distance units.
Carry the result from part (a) into part (b) and divide by the time unit s.
Check that both final forms contain only kg, m and s.

evidence.role: Grounds expansion of force and multiplication by another base quantity

hints: Write J = N m, then expand N.
Collect the two metre factors.

walkthrough.text: Energy transferred is force multiplied by distance, so J = N m.
Replace N by kg m s^-2 to obtain (kg m s^-2)m.
Collecting metre powers gives kg m^2 s^-2.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses J = N m and replaces N by kg m s^-2
Simplifies the joule to kg m^2 s^-2

evidence.role: Directly grounds deriving power as energy transferred per unit time

hints: Use W = J/s.
Insert the part (a) form before simplifying the time powers.

walkthrough.text: Power is energy transferred divided by time, so W = J s^-1.
Carry forward J = kg m^2 s^-2 from part (a).
Multiplying by s^-1 gives kg m^2 s^-3.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses W = J s^-1 and substitutes kg m^2 s^-2 for J
Simplifies the watt to kg m^2 s^-3

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground charge as A s and multi-base-unit derivation from a supplied relationship; the prompt structure is original

hints: Find the base unit of charge before starting the longer derivation.
Rearrange for epsilon and keep the denominator grouped.

walkthrough.text: Complete the charge bridge in part (a).
Use that result twice in the numerator of the rearranged expression.
Collect the A, kg, m and s powers separately.

evidence.role: Directly grounds using A s as the SI base-unit form of charge

hints: Current uses A and time uses s.

walkthrough.text: Charge is current multiplied by time.
Current has unit A and time has unit s.
Therefore charge has base unit A s.

ai_rubric.observable: States A s as the SI base-unit form of charge

evidence.role: Directly grounds deriving epsilon from the supplied charge-force-distance relationship

hints: Make epsilon the subject before substituting units.
There are two charge factors and two distance factors.

walkthrough.text: Rearrange to epsilon = Q1Q2/(4 pi F r^2).
Ignore the dimensionless 4 pi and substitute (A s)^2 for the two charges.
The denominator has units (kg m s^-2)(m^2) = kg m^3 s^-2.
Divide A^2 s^2 by kg m^3 s^-2 to obtain A^2 kg^-1 m^-3 s^(2-(-2)) = A^2 kg^-1 m^-3 s^4.
Check with fraction notation: A^2 s^4/(kg m^3) is the same result.

ai_rubric.observable: Rearranges the supplied relationship to epsilon = Q1Q2/(4 pi F r^2)
Substitutes A s for each charge, kg m s^-2 for force and m for distance
Simplifies the base units of epsilon to A^2 kg^-1 m^-3 s^4

evidence.role: Mapped leaves ground power-unit derivation and conversion to SI before calculation; the heater data and values are original

hints: Convert every value to an unprefixed SI unit before substituting.
Carry the result from each part into the next with its unit.

walkthrough.text: Convert the energy and time in part (a).
Carry 3600 J and 120 s into the supplied power relationship for part (b).
For part (c), replace J by its base-unit form and divide by s.

evidence.role: Grounds converting supplied data to SI before a calculation

hints: Kilo means 10^3.
Use the supplied conversion 1 min = 60 s.

walkthrough.text: Kilo means 10^3, so 3.6 kJ = 3.6 x 10^3 J = 3600 J.
Use the supplied conversion to change minutes to seconds: 2.0 min x 60 s/min = 120 s.
Both quantities are now ready for substitution in SI units.

ai_rubric.observable: Converts 3.6 kJ to 3.6 x 10^3 J or 3600 J

evidence.role: Grounds using power as energy transferred per unit time

hints: Use the converted values from part (a).
Divide energy by time and retain W.

walkthrough.text: Use mean power = energy transferred / time.
Substitute P = 3600 J / 120 s.
The quotient is 30 J s^-1 = 30 W.
Check: 30 W for 120 s transfers 30 x 120 = 3600 J, matching the given energy.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses mean power = energy transferred / time with the converted SI values
Calculates the mean power as 30 W

evidence.role: Directly grounds converting the watt to SI base-unit form

hints: Write W = J/s.
Expand J before combining the time powers.

walkthrough.text: A watt is a joule per second, so W = J s^-1.
A joule has base-unit form kg m^2 s^-2.
Multiplying by s^-1 gives kg m^2 s^-3.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses W = J s^-1 and replaces J with kg m^2 s^-2
Simplifies the watt to kg m^2 s^-3

quality_audit.originality: All learner contexts, wording, numerical values and the planned diagram are original. No official wording, values or diagram layouts were reproduced.
quality_audit.scope: The lesson teaches only how to express derived units in SI base-unit form by using supplied relationships. It does not teach or test equation homogeneity.
quality_audit.evidence: All eight mapped P2 leaves and their complete source-question contexts were reviewed. They ground named-unit expansion, rearrangement, charge as A s and multi-factor simplification. P1 evidence is deferred and was not inferred.
later_knowledge_excluded: applications of force, energy, power, electricity or materials beyond the supplied unit relationships
